title: NSE's FY26 Earnings: A Reality Check Before Its ₹30,000-Crore IPO
description: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) reported a significant 16% drop in net profit for FY26, falling to ₹10,302 crore from ₹12,188 crore in FY25. Operating margi.

faq.q: What caused NSE's net profit to drop in FY26?
faq.a: NSE's net profit fell by 16% in FY26 primarily due to SEBI's crackdown on speculative derivatives trading, which impacted trading volumes, and significant provisions for legacy legal settlements, including the co-location case.

faq.q: How did SEBI's derivatives crackdown affect NSE?
faq.a: SEBI's measures to strengthen the equity derivatives framework led to a moderation in trading activity across both cash and derivatives segments, directly impacting NSE's transaction charge revenue, which is a major contributor to its top line.

faq.q: What was the impact of legal settlements on NSE's financials?
faq.a: NSE made substantial provisions for legal settlements, notably ₹1,391.21 crore related to the co-location case, which significantly impacted its net profit for FY26. Other settlements, like ₹643 crore for the Trading Access Point architecture, also contributed to expenses.

faq.q: Is the ₹30,000-crore NSE IPO still on track?
faq.a: Yes, NSE has filed its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) for an IPO estimated at ₹30,000 crore, which could be India's largest. The FY26 earnings provide a crucial data point for investors to consider ahead of its listing.

faq.q: What does the decline in operating margin signify for NSE?
faq.a: The sharp fall in NSE's operating margin from 74% to 67% indicates a weakening in the profitability of its core operations. This suggests that the cost of generating revenue has increased, or revenue growth has slowed more than expenses.

faq.q: Will NSE receive funds from its IPO?
faq.a: No, the NSE IPO is entirely an Offer for Sale (OFS). This means existing shareholders will be selling their shares, and the National Stock Exchange itself will not receive any fresh capital from the public issue.

faq.q: What are the main risks highlighted by NSE in its IPO papers?
faq.a: NSE has flagged several risks, including regulatory changes in derivatives markets, technology failures, cyberattacks, AI-related challenges, and a high concentration of revenue from its top 10 trading members.
